topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The opening frames the lecture around understanding cancer treatment approaches and comparing their modes of action.

topics.label: Surgery and radiotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: This material explains how local treatments control cancer and why their success depends on tumour location and extent.

topics.label: Cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: This material examines how cytotoxic drugs kill cancer cells and what limits their effectiveness and tolerability.

topics.label: Targeting hormone-dependent cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This material explains how blocking required hormonal signals can suppress breast and prostate cancer growth.

topics.label: Exploiting cell cycle checkpoint defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how missing checkpoint proteins create vulnerabilities that can be exploited to preferentially destroy cancer cells.

topics.label: PARP inhibition in BRCA-deficient cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This material explains how inhibiting PARP selectively kills cancer cells that cannot repair the resulting double-strand DNA breaks.

topics.label: Oncogene-guided therapy and kinase inhibition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics develop the rationale for identifying cancer-driving oncogenes and inhibiting their activity with targeted drugs.

topics.label: Kinase inhibitor limitations and resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain why kinase inhibition often requires ongoing treatment that adapts to tumour resistance rather than providing a cure.

topics.label: Antibody targeting of cancer cell surface proteins
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how antibodies recognising cell surface proteins direct therapeutic effects towards cancer cells.

topics.label: Antitumour immunity and immune checkpoint inhibition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine whether naturally occurring T-cell responses can recognise cancer and be strengthened to produce therapeutic benefit.

topics.label: Redirecting T cells towards cancer cells
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe therapies that deliberately establish tumour recognition by T cells rather than relying on an existing antitumour response.

topics.label: Treatment challenges and personalised cancer therapy
topics.groupedBecause: This material considers how matching treatments to individual tumours could improve responses despite cancer heterogeneity and resistance.

topics.label: Cancer outcome trends, prevention and early detection
topics.groupedBecause: This material evaluates improvements in cancer outcomes in light of changes in prevention and detection.

topics.label: Future treatment priorities and ethical choices
topics.groupedBecause: This material considers how future cancer care should balance therapeutic advances against patient benefit and quality of life.

topics.label: Closing reflection on childhood leukaemia treatment
topics.groupedBecause: The lecture ends with childhood leukaemia as a success story that exposes the dilemma of testing new treatments against highly effective existing therapy.
